deities: Tirthankara Rishabhanatha (Adinath), the first Tirthankara - four-faced (chaumukha) 72-inch marble image in the central sanctum

history.dynasty: Mewar (patronage of Rana Kumbha; founder Dharna Shah, Porwal Jain businessman of Ghanerao; architect Deepaka/Depa)
history.period: Construction began c. 1389 per some sources (verify - likely conflation); 1436 CE copper-plate record; main structure credited to 1439; took ~50-60 years, completed 1458/1496 per sources (verify)
history.summary: NON-HINDU (Jain - Svetambara) - KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED. One of the five holiest Jain pilgrimage sites. Built by Dharna Shah after a divine vision of a celestial vehicle (Nalini-Gulma Vimana design), under Mewar king Rana Kumbha, with architect Deepaka. The chaumukha (four-faced) Adinath idol faces all four cardinal directions. Famous as the 'forest of pillars': 1444 (some sources 1440) intricately carved marble pillars, no two alike, positioned so none blocks the deity; 29 halls, 80 domes, 24 mantapas, 44 spires, 48,000 sq ft. Maru-Gurjara architecture; the marble changes shade through the day. Address records the site as Desuri, Sadri (Ranakpur Rd) 306702 in Pali district; CSV town 'Ranakpur' is the village name - acceptable. No camera/mobile inside before noon for tourists (verify current rules).

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple (Chaumukha/Adinath Temple)
town_description: Ranakpur is a village in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, set in a forested valley on the western flank of the Aravalli Range near the Magai river, about 90 km from Udaipur on the Udaipur-Jodhpur route. It is famous almost entirely for its Jain temple complex, which also contains the Surya Narayan and Amba Mata temples.

travel.road: On the Udaipur-Jodhpur highway route via Desuri; Ranakpur Rd, Sadri 306702 (verify).

visitor_information.opening_hours: Devotees/worship 6 am-7 pm; tourists 12 pm-5 pm. Entry free for Indians, Rs 200 for foreigners; camera fee Rs 100; no shorts/sleeveless - clothing available for rent (verify current rules). Open on Mahavira Jayanti.
